headline: Ginkgo and OpenAI report autonomous biology experiments at scale using GPT-5
summary: In February 2026, Ginkgo Bioworks connected GPT-5 to its cloud lab, running 36,000 experimental conditions across six iterative cycles where AI designed, executed, and learned from physical biology experiments.
details: Ginkgo Bioworks connected OpenAI's GPT-5 to its cloud laboratory in February 2026, conducting 36,000 experimental conditions over six iterative cycles. The AI autonomously designed, executed, and learned from these physical biological experiments.

This closed-loop biological experimentation at such a large scale signifies a shift for AI from purely analytical roles to active, autonomous empirical research. It represents a significant advancement in the application of AI in scientific discovery.

The success of this collaboration suggests a future where laboratories could operate with AI iteratively planning and running wet-lab experiments. This would require limited human direction, potentially accelerating research timelines dramatically.
caption:
AI just ran 36,000 biology experiments autonomously. Ginkgo Bioworks and OpenAI leveraged GPT-5 to design, execute, and learn from physical biological experiments at scale.

Ginkgo Bioworks connected OpenAI's GPT-5 to its cloud laboratory in February 2026, conducting 36,000 experimental conditions over six iterative cycles. The AI autonomously designed, executed, and learned from these physical biological experiments.

This closed-loop biological experimentation at such a large scale signifies a shift for AI from purely analytical roles to active, autonomous empirical research. It represents a significant advancement in the application of AI in scientific discovery.

The success of this collaboration suggests a future where laboratories could operate with AI iteratively planning and running wet-lab experiments. This would require limited human direction, potentially accelerating research timelines dramatically.
